name: Iranian Army (Artesh)
summary: Artesh (Iran's regular army), Day 241. More visible this window: its Navy announced new units in the Sea of Oman and Arabian Sea (13 Oct), its chief of staff said US warships will not be allowed in the Gulf 'under any circumstances' (24 Oct), and it claims to have shot down a US LUCAS drone over Bandar Abbas (25 Oct; unverified). In October Artesh chief Sayyari spoke of having 'struck blows against enemy vessels'. No joint Artesh–IRGC operational statement.

recent_signals.headline: Artesh Navy claims (27, 29, 30 Oct): 'rogue' tankers hit mines 'east of the strait'; it 'struck and destroyed' an 'enemy unmanned vessel' (30 Oct; CENTCOM: FALSE, all US USVs accounted for); Rear Adm. Moghadam claims 'more than 20' attacks on US warships in the war. Army chief Hatami attended the leader's first reported meeting with all three service chiefs (31 Oct, written statement). Spokesman Akraminia: a new US attack would spread the war to 'a much wider geographical area'. Artesh and IRGC claims contradicted each other (1 vs 3 vs 4 tankers; 'east' vs 'southern route'). (CLAIMED; intel KIN-A3/A6/B2)

Iran's regular Navy announced (13 Oct) new units deployed east of the strait 'across the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea' for 'real time surveillance', warning ships not to switch off AIS; Armed Forces Chief of Staff Abdollahi (24 Oct): 'We will not allow U.S. military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time'; the Army claims it downed a US LUCAS drone over Bandar Abbas (25 Oct; US silent). (CONFIRMED statements; LUCAS CLAIMED; intel KIN-A3/A6)

**Artesh chief of staff/joint coordinator Maj. Gen. Habibollah Sayyari (11 Oct): 'We have struck blows against enemy vessels. If anything else happens against Iran, we will strike them again.'** — a general statement with no referent (Press TV ran it as a conditional threat), not an admission of specific merchant-ship strikes; Artesh threatened pre-emptive strikes on US positions (7 Oct, CBS); army commander: 50+ units deployed on borders (10 Oct). (Al Jazeera, The National, CBS) — CONFIRMED as statements. Bears on the artesh 'specific operational deployment' and 'joint Artesh–IRGC statement' triggers: convergence of line (both claim the campaign) without a joint statement — not fired.

**B5 ARTESH SPOKESPERSON BRIG. GEN. AKRAMINIA WARNED IN IRNA INTERVIEW OF 'SURPRISING OPTIONS' IF ADVERSARIES MAKE ANOTHER 'MISCALCULATION'** — saying any future aggression would take the conflict into areas 'the enemy has not anticipated' (CONFIRMED RHETORIC — IRNA primary). Distinct from Pezeshkian's civilian 'never bow' framing and from IRGC drill-based readiness signaling. An Artesh spokesperson making a 'surprising options' claim alongside an active IRGC drill is the cleanest signal yet of coordinated kinetic-readiness messaging across both Iranian military pillars exactly as the Trump-Xi joint statement was being issued (Iran 'can never have a nuclear weapon'). **The brief notes this as additional escalation rhetoric on the Iran side**: Tehran signaling readiness from BOTH Artesh and IRGC channels even as China rhetorically aligns with the US on the nuclear-weapons line.
recent_signals.verification: Akraminia 'surprising options' = CONFIRMED RHETORIC (IRNA primary, single source but on-record Artesh spokesperson statement). No operational deployment named or observed.

recent_signals.headline: **THE ARTESH — NOT THE IRGC — IS BEING CREDITED WITH THE GULF STRIKES, AND THIS IS A GENUINE UNRESOLVED ANOMALY.** IRNA and Mehr credit 'Iran's Army' with the missile and drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait: 'The army's ground forces targeted the HIMARS missile systems of the US terrorist army stationed at the Arifjan base in Kuwait with surface-to-surface missiles.' Press TV attributes to the Army one-way drones against Camp Arifjan, Al Udairi Camp and Ahmad Al Jaber Air Base. **An ARTESH spokesman, Mohammad Akrami Nia, is issuing the doctrinal statements** — 'War will continue until full deterrence is achieved' and 'Rationality dictates that the war continue' — and the Army declared that 'no equipment intended for use against Iran can transit the Strait of Hormuz.' The IRGC is simultaneously claiming Bahrain, the Hormuz tanker strikes and Syria. **Regular-army units publicly credited with cross-border strikes on US bases, with an Artesh rather than IRGC spokesman issuing war aims, is NOT the normal division of labour.** Two readings, and they cannot yet be discriminated: **(a)** burden-sharing because IRGC missile and launcher inventories are degraded after ten nights of strikes on launch sites; **(b)** a deliberate rebalancing of institutional credit inside a regime with a contested leadership — which would connect directly to the elite split and to Vahidi's reported centrality. **ISW's 20 July report does NOT mention Artesh involvement at all and describes the IRGC as the dominant offensive force.** Flagged as unresolved and tracked. REPORTED.
